notes: Each catalog ID has a distinct BoardModel name and an explicitly selected hardware target. Shared protocol mechanics follow exact manufacturer evidence, not name similarity.

All eight new OLED targets and T-2CAN have authored native Xtensa MMIO probes. The three TFT Deck variants also have native guest display/GPIO probes; Pro has protocol tests. None has an official binary boot or physical-hardware validation claim.
Shared SSD1306/SH1106 controllers are allocated only for opted-in boards. No CPU, bus, tick or global peripheral route changes were made.
Every documented physical TF slot uses the platform prepared 64 MiB FAT32 policy. Smaller deterministic test images verify real SPI block read/write and supply-cycle persistence.

The SX1262 packet subset on three TFT Deck variants is tested through correct board pins, power, reset, matching configuration, RX buffer, TX capture and IRQ. Other profiles do not expose radio capability merely because a chip is physically present.
Unknown dates remain unknown. Storefront dates are low-confidence ordering proxies; T-2Can uses its explicit V1.0 manufacturer version date.

Three more exact screen targets share the private DCS transport with explicit source profiles. CST226SE 8-bit reports and CST816D family ID/report behavior are separate; all three have real Xtensa display/GPIO probes and I2C pin rejection tests.

Original TWR Rev1.x and the two Plus revisions keep separate OLED/encoder/PMU maps. Original schematic VBAT gating leaves VDD/I2C/RAM live. MVSR selects the exact complete storefront kit; the separately sold backplate has no CPU.
